newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dlr ends stronger ahead of Ontario budget.
newsitem.headline: Canada dlr ends stronger ahead of Ontario budget.

text.p: * Canada's dollar ended stronger at C$1.3790 (US$0.7158) on Monday from Friday's close of C$1.3805 (US$0.7243) ahead of Tuesday's budget from Canada's most-populous province. * Traders said the Canadian dollar strengthened on broad-based buying ahead of the fiscal 1997/98 budget for the Province of Ontario.
"We got to C$1.3783 (US$0.7255) in Singapore, and then it sold off on the Bre-X story," said Reid Farrill, corporate foreign exchange adviser for CIBC Wood Gundy.

Economists have said they are predicting that Ontario's 1996/97 deficit would drop below C$7.0 billion government and some have said the government could wipe out its deficit by fiscal 1999/2000, one year ahead of plan.

The provincial government has delivered 15 percent of a promised 30 percent tax cut by 1999, and some economists have speculated the timetable for the remaining 15 percent cut could be accelerated in Tuesday's budget.
On the crosses, Canada's dollar rose to 1.2567 marks from Friday's close of 1.2520 and edged up to 91.80 yen from 91.57 yen.
